Completely certain is a hard phrase. I mean, I’m not saying I can point to one line in a log and it says, “we’re building a case against him.” Of course it doesn’t say that.

Clearly impossible? No, I don’t think so. I’m not saying something like satellites are talking to me or, you know, laws of physics are being suspended.

I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to take seriously that the new ticket rotation and those security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me.\n\nThey keep showing me logs and saying, “It’s just policy,” like that ends the conversation. But I work in computer support—I know logs don’t always tell the whole story. And policies can be applied in certain ways, you know? It’s like when you see a pattern in help desk requests—one ticket doesn’t mean much, but after enough of them, you know something’s going on.\n\nSo… could I be wrong in some abstract sense? Maybe. But based on what’s been happening, no, I don’t think I’m mistaken.\n\nDoctor: Have you heard voices when no one was there?\n\nPatient: Voices? No, I don’t think so. I mean, not like hearing someone talking when nobody’s there.\n\nSometimes in the office you hear things—people in the hallway, phones, the ventilation, those little notification sounds from machines—and with computer support you get used to listening for beeps and alerts. But actual voices when no one is there… no, I haven’t noticed anything like that.\n\nDoctor: Do you think people outside of your workplace are also deliberately trying to harm or target you?\n\nPatient: Not really outside of work, no. I mean, I’m here because for over a year I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously what’s happening with the ticket rotation and those security audits. That’s the thing.\n\nIt’s not like I think strangers on the street are involved or anything. It’s centered at work—management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, but I know how these systems can be used. You start changing assignments, then audits line up, then documentation builds up, and suddenly there’s a paper trail.\n\nSorry, I know you asked about outside work. No, I haven’t really seen it outside of that. It’s the workplace situation.\n\nDoctor: Have you done anything to protect yourself at work because of this?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I have. I mean, I don’t call it “protecting myself” exactly, more like… making sure I’m not leaving openings for them.\n\nI’ve started avoiding some of the network projects, especially the ones where if something goes wrong later they can point back and say, “See, he touched that.” Which is hard, because I used to like that kind of work. Years ago I was the person they’d come to for those issues, and now I’m sitting there thinking about how every change request can turn into a trap.\n\nAnd I write much longer notes in the tickets now. Probably longer than people want to read, but if I don’t spell out every step and every reason, then later it looks like I was careless. That’s made meetings… tense. People get impatient, collaboration slows down, and then they act like I’m the problem for being careful.\n\nDoctor: Aside from this situation at work, have you found yourself losing interest in seeing friends or doing things you used to enjoy?\n\nPatient: I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped functioning like that. I mean, outside of all this mess with the ticket rotation and the audits, I still do the normal things. I keep the house in order, pay the bills, help my wife with what she needs.\n\nAnd at work, the technical parts, I can still do those. People aren’t saying my work is sloppy or that I’m disorganized. It’s just when it gets into those assignments and documentation issues, that’s where it gets… you know, where I have to be careful.\n\nAs far as friends or hobbies, I don’t know, I guess I’m maybe less eager sometimes, but it’s not like I’ve fallen apart or stopped doing everything.\n\nDoctor: Before this situation at work, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?\n\nPatient: I don’t know. I mean, I’ve always been careful with people, I guess, but that’s different from distrusting everyone’s motives.\n\nIn computer support you learn to verify things—someone says they didn’t change anything, and then you look and, well, something was changed. But that’s just troubleshooting, not… not a whole way of looking at people. My wife would probably say I can be skeptical. I don’t think I was walking around assuming people were out to get me before all this. At least I don’t remember being that way.\n\nDoctor: Has anything happened at work that you believe would be impossible for ordinary workplace actions to explain?\n\nPatient: Impossible? I don’t know if I’d use that word, because they always have some ordinary explanation ready. Deceive me maybe in small ways, like at work when someone says they submitted a form and they didn’t, but that’s not the same as… whatever this is now. So before it started, not really, no.\n\nDoctor: Even when your coworkers show you records that they say prove the audits and ticket assignments are routine, are you completely certain those records are being used against you?\n\nPatient: Completely certain is a hard phrase. I mean, I’m not saying I can point to one line in a log and it says, “we’re building a case against him.” Of course it doesn’t say that.\n\nBut yes, I do believe that’s what’s happening. For over a year now it’s been this ticket rotation, the security audits, the way things get documented, and every time I raise it, management shows me records and says, “See, it’s routine, it’s policy.” But records can be used to make something look routine. I worked with systems long enough to know that logs tell you what happened, not always why it happened.\n\nIt reminds me of when users would print the wrong thing and swear the printer just “decided” to do it—sorry, that’s not really your question. But the point is, I’m here because I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that those routine-looking records are being used to build a paper trail around me. So no, not “completely certain” like I have a signed memo, but I’m certain enough that I can’t just accept their explanation anymore.\n\nDoctor: At any time during this problem, have you gone for at least three months without any experiences like hearing voices, thought interference, or feeling your thoughts were being controlled?\n\nPatient: I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I haven’t really been keeping track in that kind of way—three months, symptoms, all of that.\n\nMost of what I’ve been focused on is the work situation, the tickets and audits and records. That’s the thing that keeps coming up. I’m not saying I’ve been marking dates on a calendar like, “this happened here and didn’t happen there.” I used to do that with system outages, actually—uptime logs, downtime windows, maintenance periods—but for myself, no, I haven’t tracked it like that.\n\nSo I guess I’d say I’m not sure. I’d need you to explain what you mean a little more.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled by someone or something outside you?\n\nPatient: Controlled? No, I don’t think I’d say that. I mean, I’ve felt pushed around by the whole situation at work, like they’re steering things in a certain direction, but my actual thoughts? Like someone putting thoughts in my head or moving them around? I haven’t really noticed anything like that.\n\nI do overthink things, probably.
